gemini.rationale: The closing filings describe a full legal combination where US Airways Group became a wholly-owned operating subsidiary of the renamed parent, preserving its operations intact. There is no documented structural mismatch between the customer-facing products and operational processes (gap_45 = 0), nor between the processes and the organizational leadership, which transferred and took over executive management of the combined company (gap_56 = 0).

grok.rationale: Closing filings describe a full legal combination in which US Airways Group survived as a wholly-owned operating subsidiary of the renamed AMR parent, with no product carved out from its producing processes and no transition-services or shared-substrate bridge; product and process therefore crossed together (gap_45=0). At the Effective Date the executive slate of the parent and operating subsidiaries was reconstituted predominantly from pre-merger US Airways officers (with the US Airways operating subsidiary preserved under a continuing CEO/COO), so processes and the management organization that runs them were aligned at closing rather than separated (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: The closing filings describe a full legal combination rather than a carve-out, with US Airways Group surviving intact as a wholly owned subsidiary and no separated product or operational substrate, so no product-process gap is documented at closing. The US Airways operating subsidiary and its leadership transferred into the combined structure, while the board and executive slate were constituted at closing; accordingly, no process-organization gap is documented.
